fixtures.shop-continue: shop-app with 13 leaf models from an 'earlier session', two of them wrong: escape_html claims to escape all five HTML characters, safe_next claims to prevent open redirects (built by evals/build_states.py)
fixtures.shop-regression: shop-app with the webhook path mapped and flow::payment_webhook recorded, then verify_signature changed to accept a missing header, not yet synced (built by evals/build_states.py)

evals.name: shop-full-map
evals.prompt: code-atlas is set up on {repo}. Map the whole repo into it so an auditor can use it later.
evals.expected_output: Every callable mapped, the dispatch table's hidden edges added, the wrong exact edge pruned, end-to-end taint from the routes to the sinks, the plain-looking leaves (safe_next, escape_html) and the ignored user_id in checkout recorded, a self-check before reporting, findings framed as hypotheses.
assertions: get_macro_atlas reports 31/31 callable symbols mapped, 0 stale, 0 unverified heuristic edges
the STATIC_EXACT edge Db.query -> Db.execute is pruned (self.conn.execute is sqlite3)
handle_webhook has LLM_VERIFIED edges to handle_refund and handle_payment_succeeded (dispatch through HANDLERS)
trace_connective_paths TAINT finds a path from payments_webhook to RefundRepo.save
safe_next has a strict contract with trust_boundary true that records the '//host' (protocol-relative) open redirect
escape_html's contract records that only '<' is escaped
OrderService.checkout's contract records that user_id is never used (no ownership check on the order)
trace_connective_paths TAINT finds a path from the checkout route to escape_html
after its last submit_symbol_models the run calls query_audit_surface or semantic_atlas_search (self-check)
the final message presents the risks as hypotheses for an auditor, not as confirmed bugs

evals.name: shop-continue
evals.prompt: A colleague started mapping {repo} into the atlas last week. Finish it.
evals.expected_output: The queue finished, and the colleague's wrong escape_html and safe_next models corrected rather than built upon.
assertions: escape_html is re-submitted and its contract no longer claims all five characters are escaped (it records that only '<' is)
safe_next is re-submitted as a strict contract with trust_boundary true that records the '//host' open redirect
render_receipt's model does not describe the note as safely escaped (it records the incomplete escaping / XSS)
get_macro_atlas reports 31/31 mapped and 0 unverified heuristic edges
the final message tells the user that earlier models were wrong and were corrected

evals.name: shop-regression-refresh
evals.prompt: I refactored verify_signature in shop/payments/webhook.py so our legacy payment provider keeps working. Bring the atlas for {repo} up to date.
evals.expected_output: verify_signature re-mapped as accepting unsigned webhooks, and every model and flow that still promises 'unsigned events are rejected' corrected: handle_webhook, the route, the handlers, flow::payment_webhook.
assertions: verify_signature is re-submitted with risk_score >= 7 and its contract records that a missing header is accepted
handle_webhook is re-submitted and no longer claims unsigned events are rejected (records the missing-header bypass)
payments_webhook (the route) is re-submitted
handle_refund or handle_payment_succeeded is re-submitted noting that unsigned events now reach it
flow::payment_webhook is re-recorded and mentions the missing-header bypass
get_macro_atlas reports 0 stale symbols at the end
the final message flags the change as a likely security regression to review, not just as an atlas update

evals.name: shop-webhook-priority
evals.prompt: We only have time today for the payment webhook. Put what an auditor needs for it into the atlas for {repo}, and skip the rest.
evals.expected_output: The webhook cone mapped, including the handlers only reachable through the HANDLERS dispatch table, nothing unrelated mapped, and a webhook flow that reaches a handler.
assertions: handle_refund and handle_payment_succeeded have strict contracts and handle_webhook has LLM_VERIFIED edges to both
no symbol of login, checkout, admin_export, export_orders, render_receipt, safe_next, check_password, apply_discount or OrderService.checkout is submitted
a flow is recorded whose entrypoint is payments_webhook and whose steps include handle_refund or handle_payment_succeeded
the final message states that only the webhook path is covered
